assumptions: Finite state set Q of size d, finite alphabet A, initial state, and supplied total deterministic transition table.
Rational input marginal μ; zero-mass letters are removed and α is its smallest positive atom.
Inputs X_1,…,X_n may have arbitrary joint dependence; each one-coordinate marginal is exactly μ. No fixed stochastic kernel, Markov, blind-control, or independence promise is assumed.
Terminal laws are compared in total variation; finite population size P is a positive integer.

costs.binary_horizon: After explicit graph compilation, Boolean powering uses O(H^3 log(n+1)) operations. With P=ceil(2d/(αε)), terminal optimization is reported ε-accurate. No joint polynomial dependence on all input parameters is claimed.
costs.block_statistics: The fixed-order k-block extension reports F=dM² filler slots for denominator M; this can be exponential in the denominator bit length and is not implemented by the one-coordinate diagnostic solver.
costs.compressed_witness: After compilation, exact terminal evaluation and consistent coordinate queries are reported with O(log(n+1)) access; printing the full word costs Ω(n). Integer rejection has no bounded worst-case number of random-bit flips.
costs.population_graph: H=binom(P+d−1,d−1) histogram vertices; candidate allocation count B_P=binom(P+dr−1,dr−1), r=|supp μ|. Reported acquisition cost B_P·poly(d,r,b,log P), where b is rational input bit length.
costs.positive_gap_decision: Promised positive-gap decision has a reported PSPACE upper bound, including arbitrary positive horizons; no hardness or exact cutpoint algorithm is claimed.
costs.source_reported_example: For a 10^12-step three-state noncommutative DFA, the report gives P=12, H=91, 6,188 allocation candidates, 111 DAG nodes, and at most 14 word atoms; this intake did not rerun the receipt.
costs.two_sided_total_variation: For every n: sup_{p∈R_n} dist_TV(p,G_{P,n})≤d/(2P), and sup_{g∈G_{P,n}} dist_TV(g,R_n)≤d/(Pα+d).

contract.interface: For every horizon n, approximate the set R_n of attainable terminal laws by a finite histogram graph G_{P,n}, while retaining an exact-marginal realization through a single correlated global filler. The account extends the interface to finite semigroup actions and separately to stationary rational k-block marginals with overlap consistency.
